stem: A client is unable to bear any body weight during a bed-to-chair transfer. Which transfer method is most appropriate?

options.A: Use a full-body mechanical lift with the appropriate sling and trained staff assistance
options.B: Use a sit-to-stand lift even though the client cannot bear weight
options.C: Have one staff member manually lift the client
options.D: Ask the client to attempt the transfer independently without an assistive device

rationale: OSHA safe-patient-handling guidance states that mechanical lifting equipment should be used for patients who cannot support their own weight. A full-body sling lift is specifically used for non-weight-bearing patients, whereas a sit-to-stand device requires the patient to be able to bear some body weight.
educational_objective: Select a full-body mechanical lift for a non-weight-bearing client and avoid unsafe manual lifting or a sit-to-stand device that requires weight-bearing ability.
source_document_title: Hospitals eTool — Patient Care Unit: Work-related Musculoskeletal Disorders
source_locator: Recognized Controls and Work Practices > Mechanical lift equipment > Sit-to-Stand Device and Sling-Type Full Lift
source_claim_supported: Mechanical lifting equipment is used for patients who cannot support their own weight; sit-to-stand devices require some weight-bearing ability, while full-body sling lifts are used for non-weight-bearing patients.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Basic Care and Comfort, printed p.11 / PDF p.15; detailed content: Mobility/Immobility, printed p.36 / PDF p.39
correction_summary: Specified complete inability to bear weight so the correct device is uniquely determined, distinguished a full-body lift from a sit-to-stand lift, and replaced vague/random transfer distractors with clinically meaningful alternatives.
audit_findings: A directly matches OSHA guidance for a non-weight-bearing patient. B requires some weight-bearing ability; C exposes staff and client to avoidable manual-lifting risk; D is unsafe for a client who cannot bear weight. NCSBN Mobility/Immobility supports the Basic Care and Comfort mapping. No second answer remains.
